result.title: When Agents Play Differently: Localizing Human--Agent Behavioral Divergence with Conditional Distributional Testing
result.summary: Evaluating whether artificial agents behave like humans requires comparing not just average outcomes but entire behavioral distributions across diverse contexts. We propose a stratified framework that computes nonparametric discrepancy statistics within contextual cells, and discovers subgroup rules identifying where agent behavior departs from human play. We show that session-level metrics dominated by win/loss outcomes offer little signal beyond mean comparisons, whereas process-level metrics such as move efficiency reveal genuine behavioral differences. Applied to a commercial match-3 game, it uncovers patterns invisible to aggregate metrics: a playtesting bot is diverging substantially from humans in certain game modes, while showing no detectable divergence in others. We release our implementation as open source to support reproducibility and adoption.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出分层条件分布检验框架，在上下文单元内计算非参数差异统计并挖掘子群规则，用于定位智能体与人类行为分歧的位置；在三消游戏中发现会话级输赢指标几乎无额外信号，而过程级指标能揭示特定模式下的真实差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按情境分层、定位差异子群」的检验思路可能可供核查，用于判断 latent 推理步骤（THINK/LOOK/STOP）在哪些情境下带来真实收益、哪些只体现在均值层面；但该工作不涉及视觉推理或内部状态，指标需自行改造。
